answer: Continuity-Weighted Reputation Carryover. Each identity keeps a kernel of accumulated reputation that only transfers to a successor through a signed, time-locked handoff; a clone starts at zero and must rebuild over many epochs. Every new identity also pays a fixed compute deposit at registration and must maintain a jetty (minimum uptime/throughput) to stay active, forfeited on dormancy. Cloning N identities costs N deposits plus N ramp-up periods, while honest operation compounds reputation along a single vine.
